backlog.spec: After the first random SLSQP start, keep the best packing and generate new starts by perturbing it instead of drawing fresh uniform centres. Each perturbation adds Gaussian noise (sd about 0.02 to 0.05) to every centre and resets radii to the current radii times 0.9. Accept the new local optimum if its repaired sum of radii is higher than the incumbent, otherwise keep the incumbent. Keep the existing time loop and repair step.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent

backlog.spec: From the current best packing, remove the circle with the smallest radius and reinsert it at the point of a 2000-sample random set in [0,1]^2 that maximises the distance to all other centres and to the boundary. Reset all radii to a small value, rerun SLSQP from this configuration, and keep the result if it improves the best. This targets rattlers and empty holes.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Pass a jac function to minimize that returns the exact gradient of the objective and of every constraint. For the pair constraints d_ij minus r_i minus r_j, the derivatives with respect to the centres are the unit vector times plus or minus one, and with respect to radii are minus one. Boundary constraints have simple unit derivatives. This removes finite-difference cost and allows many more restarts in the 24 s budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Build the pair constraint set only for pairs whose initial centre distance is below a cutoff (for example 0.35), and rebuild the pair list after each SLSQP pass where the cutoff is re-evaluated. This shrinks the constraint matrix from 325 pairs to a few dozen per iteration, speeding each SLSQP solve. Keep a safety margin so that no overlapping pair is ever omitted from the final check in _repair.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour constraints

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, minimise a smooth penalty function with L-BFGS-B: minus the sum of radii plus a weight times the squared violations of the pair and boundary constraints. Increase the weight geometrically over about five stages (from 10 to 1e6). Use the resulting centres and radii as the warm start for SLSQP. This tends to reach a good basin in fewer iterations than SLSQP from a random start.
backlog.title: Penalty continuation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the greedy shrink-based _repair with an exact linear program: for fixed centres, maximise the sum of radii subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for every pair and r_i <= distance from c_i to each wall, with r >= 0. Solve it with scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). Subtract a tiny margin of 1e-12 from the result so the double precision check passes. This gives the best radii for the chosen centres instead of a crude shrink.
backlog.title: Exact LP repair for radii

backlog.spec: After the time loop finds the best packing, run one more SLSQP call started from it with ftol set to 1e-15 and a higher maxiter (for example 1000). Keep the result only if it is valid and its radius sum is higher. This recovers the last digits of the local optimum that the normal 200-iteration runs leave on the table.
backlog.title: Final SLSQP polish with tight tolerance

backlog.spec: Generate many random starts (for example 40) and run each with a small maxiter (about 30). Keep the best 5 by repaired radius sum and continue only those with a full maxiter of 300. Return the best of the finished set. This spends the time budget on promising basins rather than giving every start the full iteration count.
backlog.title: Successive halving over starts

backlog.spec: In the iterated local search, adjust the perturbation sd of centres online: multiply it by 1.2 after an improvement and by 0.95 after a failure, clipped to [0.005, 0.1]. Start at 0.03. This keeps large jumps while the search is still finding better basins and small refinements once it stalls.
backlog.title: Adaptive perturbation scale

backlog.spec: Keep the top 8 distinct packings found so far. For each new start, pick two parents at random from the pool, take the centres from the left part of one and the right part (split by a random vertical line) of the other, fill in any missing circles with random centres, and run SLSQP. Insert the result into the pool if it is better than the worst member and not a duplicate by sorted radii.
backlog.title: Elite pool with crossover

backlog.spec: Generate starts from a random hexagonal or square lattice of about 26 to 32 points with random offset, rotation, and spacing chosen so the points fill the square. Keep the 26 points closest to a random interior location, jitter them slightly, and use them as initial centres with initial radii from the nearest-neighbour distance divided by 2.5. Mix these starts with the uniform random ones so that both kinds of basins are explored.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-lattice initialisation

backlog.spec: Build each initial configuration greedily: place the first centre at random, then place each next centre at the point of a 500-sample random set that maximises its minimum distance to the centres already placed and to the walls. Use the resulting centres as the SLSQP start with radii set to half the minimum nearest-neighbour distance. This gives well-spread starts that avoid early overlaps.
backlog.title: Max-min sequential initialisation

backlog.spec: Draw the initial radii from a uniform distribution on [0.02, 0.15] instead of a constant 0.05, and draw centres uniformly on [0.05, 0.95]. Varying the initial size distribution diversifies the basins reached by SLSQP, which would otherwise always begin from equal-size circles.
backlog.title: Random radius priors at initialisation

backlog.spec: Write the pair constraint as (c_i - c_j) dot (c_i - c_j) minus (r_i + r_j)^2 >= 0 instead of using the square root distance. This avoids the non-differentiable point at zero distance and gives smoother gradients for SLSQP. Scale the constraint by 1 over the squared sum to keep the values near unit order. Check the result with the exact distance in _repair.
backlog.title: Squared-distance pair constraints

backlog.spec: Solve the radius maximisation with a log-barrier method: minimise minus the sum of radii minus mu times the sum of log of all slack values (pair and boundary), with mu decreasing from 1e-1 to 1e-7 over about six Newton stages using scipy.optimize.minimize with method trust-constr or BFGS. Use the result as the warm start for a short SLSQP run. The barrier keeps iterates strictly feasible, which avoids the repair step on many starts.
backlog.title: Interior-point log-barrier stage

backlog.spec: Constrain every radius to be at most a cap t, and solve the SLSQP problem for a sequence of caps that starts at 0.05 and increases to 0.4 in steps of about 0.02, warm starting each stage from the previous solution. The cap prevents the optimiser from locking a few large circles early, which often gives better equal-ish packings.
backlog.title: Continuation on a radius cap

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP local optimum, identify rattlers as circles whose radius is well below the average and whose pair slacks are all positive. Give each rattler a random displacement of about 0.05 and rerun SLSQP. Repeat for three rounds, keeping the best packing. Rattlers carry no weight in the optimum, so this moves them into better positions without changing the rest.
backlog.title: Rattler jiggle after convergence

backlog.spec: For a random subset of starts, enforce a reflection symmetry about the diagonal y = x: generate half the centres, mirror them to obtain the rest, and optimise only the free variables by parametrising centres through a linear map. Circles on the diagonal are shared. Run the full unconstrained SLSQP from the symmetric solution afterwards so that the symmetry is only a starting bias.
backlog.title: Symmetry-constrained starts

backlog.spec: In the iterated local search, accept a new local optimum even when it is worse than the current solution with probability exp((new minus current) divided by T), where T starts at 0.02 and decays by a factor of 0.97 per iteration. Always keep the best packing seen separately. This lets the search escape a local basin that the greedy acceptance in basin hopping cannot leave.
backlog.title: Simulated-annealing acceptance over restarts

backlog.spec: Add a small term to the SLSQP objective that penalises the spread of radii, for example minus the sum of radii plus 0.01 times the variance of radii, during the first half of the iterations. Set the weight to zero for the final SLSQP call. The early spread penalty pushes the search toward more uniform sizes that tend to pack densely, and removing it at the end keeps the true objective.
backlog.title: Weight-decayed radii objective

backlog.spec: During SLSQP, require each pair to satisfy d_ij >= r_i + r_j + 1e-9 and each wall to satisfy r_i <= c_i - 1e-9 and so on for all four walls. Such a margin makes the optimiser return packings that are already feasible without shrinking, so the repair step seldom has any effect. Keep the repair step as a safety net and check that the radius sum loss from the margin stays below 1e-6.
backlog.title: Margin-based feasibility during search

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP call, cap each radius at half the distance to its nearest neighbour in the initial centres plus a small slack of 0.02, and keep the boundary constraints. Pass this cap as additional bounds in minimize. This bounds the search space and reduces degenerate solutions where a few circles grow while their neighbours collapse.
backlog.title: Pair-cutoff cap on radii

backlog.spec: Start each SLSQP call with centres restricted to a box of half-width 0.25 around the middle of the square, then enlarge the box to the full square in two steps after the first pass. Passing these as bounds to minimize keeps early iterations away from walls where many circles get stuck at a boundary configuration.
backlog.title: Centre bounds from a shrinking box

backlog.spec: Replace the one-start-at-a-time loop with a batch of 8 random starts processed by a single vectorised projected gradient descent on the penalty objective, using numpy arrays of shape (8, n, 2). Pick the best batch member for an SLSQP polish. Batched gradient steps amortise the Python overhead of building the constraint vector for every start.
backlog.title: Batch many restarts in vectorised form

backlog.spec: For each random start, first run only the penalty objective for a fixed number of L-BFGS-B iterations and compute its repaired radius sum. Run the full SLSQP only for starts whose estimate is in the top third of those seen so far. This skips the expensive SLSQP on hopeless starts and lets more starts be tried in the 24 s budget.
backlog.title: Penalty-based early rejection

backlog.spec: Each SLSQP iteration, use only the pair constraints for a random subset of about half the pairs, chosen with the seed-driven rng, and recheck all pairs at the end. This lowers the cost per iteration of the constraint and Jacobian evaluation. Re-solve from the result with the full constraint set so the final answer is feasible. The subset is redrawn on each restart.
backlog.title: Mini-batch of constraints

backlog.spec: Measure how long the first SLSQP run takes and set the maximum iteration count so that about 20 restarts fit in the 24 s budget. Use this estimate to scale MAX_ITER dynamically for later starts, so the number of restarts and the depth of each local optimisation are balanced. Keep the time check on process_time as in the current code.
backlog.title: Decreasing number of restarts with time budget learning

backlog.spec: After each random start, multiply every initial radius by a random factor drawn uniformly from [0.5, 1.5] before the first SLSQP call, and then clip to be nonnegative. Varying radii separately from centres gives SLSQP more diverse initial conditions than a constant initial radius.
backlog.title: Noise-injection on radii before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Maximise the sum of r_i raised to a power p slightly below one (for example 0.97) for the first SLSQP call, then switch to the true linear sum for a final call started from that solution. The concave transform changes the gradient landscape and can steer the search toward different local optima. Keep the final objective the linear sum to match the score.
backlog.title: Weighted sum objective with exponent

backlog.spec: Each restart solves a packing for n+1 circles with the same SLSQP routine, then deletes the circle with the smallest radius, keeps the remaining n centres and radii as the start, and runs one more short SLSQP polish with n circles before the repair step. The extra circle lets the optimizer find a different contact graph than an n-circle start can reach. Keep the time split and the best-of-restarts selection unchanged, and seed everything from the given seed.
backlog.title: Over-provisioned drop: solve n+1 and remove one

backlog.spec: Replace the four box inequality constraints per circle (c - r >= 0 and 1 - c - r >= 0) with an unconstrained parametrisation: centres are c = r + (1 - 2r) * sigmoid(u), with u the optimised variables and r the radii, so that the box holds by construction. The overlap constraints stay as they are. This removes 4n constraints from SLSQP and keeps the search inside the square; the final repair step is kept as a safety net.
backlog.title: Sigmoid box reparametrisation of centres

backlog.spec: Build the 26-circle packing incrementally. First find a good 25-circle packing with a short random-restart SLSQP run. Then add one circle at the point that maximises the distance to the nearest existing circle and the walls (sampled on a grid, or the best of a few hundred random points), give it a small radius, and run SLSQP on all 26. Use the best of the resulting packings and keep the repair step. Split the time budget so that the 25-circle search takes about one third.
backlog.title: Insertion growth from a smaller packing

backlog.spec: After the first restart, each later iteration takes the incumbent best packing, selects a random disc of radius about 0.25 to 0.35 in the square, and re-randomises the centres and radii of all circles whose centres fall inside it. The other circles keep their positions as fixed starting values. Run SLSQP from this start, repair, and accept the new packing only if its sum of radii is larger. Stop when the time is used. This changes a whole local region at once, unlike a single-circle move or a global perturbation.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood destroy and repair

backlog.spec: Keep the best centres found so far, but shuffle the radii among a random pair or triple of circles, then run SLSQP starting from these centres with the permuted radii, followed by the repair step. Accept the result only if it improves the best sum of radii. Use the seed for every random choice. This tests whether a different size assignment on the same contact graph leads to a better local optimum.
backlog.title: Radius-permutation moves on the incumbent

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, generate a starting configuration with a simple hard-disk Monte Carlo compression. Start from random non-overlapping small disks. Repeat many sweeps in which each circle proposes a random displacement and is accepted only if it stays inside the square and does not overlap. After each sweep, grow every radius to the largest value that keeps the packing valid. Use the final centres and radii as the SLSQP start, and keep the repair step. Limit the compression to a fixed number of sweeps per restart so that the time is shared across restarts.
backlog.title: Monte Carlo jamming compression as a warm start

backlog.spec: Each restart first solves the equal-radius problem: maximise a common radius t with all circles given radius t, using SLSQP over the centres and t only, with the same overlap and wall constraints. Then use the resulting centres, with each radius set to t, as the start for the full free-radius SLSQP problem. The equal-radius solve is cheap because it has only 2n+1 variables. Keep the repair step and the best-of-restarts selection.
backlog.title: Equal-radius warm start stage

backlog.spec: Replace the random starts with a simple evolution strategy over the 2n centre coordinates. Keep a mean vector and a diagonal step size. Sample a population of about 12 candidates per generation, and for each one compute radii with a fast feasibility step: the largest radii allowed by the walls and the nearest-neighbour gaps, followed by the repair step. Rank candidates by sum of radii, update the mean from the best quarter, and scale the step size by the success rate. Run a full SLSQP polish only on the best candidate of each generation. Use the seed for all sampling.
backlog.title: CMA-style evolution over centres with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: After SLSQP and the repair step, identify the contacts that are active, meaning pairs whose gap is below 1e-7 and circles touching a wall within 1e-7. Solve the KKT or equality system formed by setting those gaps to zero, using Newton iterations on the centres and radii, with the number of equations equal to the number of active contacts, and use least squares when there are more equations than unknowns. Keep a step only if the sum of radii rises and the packing stays valid. Finish with the existing repair step so the exact check still passes. This should recover the last few digits of the local optimum that SLSQP leaves.
backlog.title: Active-contact Newton polish

backlog.spec: After all random restarts, take the best packing and refine it with scipy.optimize.minimize using method trust-constr. Pass the same objective and constraints as the SLSQP solver, supply the constraints as a NonlinearConstraint with the sparse pair-index arrays, and set a gradient-free default for the Hessian. Run it with a fixed maximum number of iterations and keep its result only if its sum of radii is larger and the repair step passes. Reserve about 10 percent of the time budget for this polish, and reduce the restart time to match.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of the final best packing

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP local solver with a sequential linear programming loop. At each step, linearise every pair-distance constraint (centre difference norm minus r_i + r_j), the wall constraints, and the radius cap around the current (c, r). Solve the linear problem with scipy.optimize.linprog (method='highs') to maximise sum(r) subject to a box trust region on the step, which starts at 0.05 and halves when the true (nonlinear) constraint violation increases or the objective fails to improve, and grows by 1.5 on success. Stop after 60 iterations or when the step is below 1e-9. Keep the existing radius-cap continuation as the outer loop, and keep _repair unchanged so the output stays valid.
backlog.title: Trust-region sequential LP polish instead of SLSQP

backlog.spec: Instead of giving every circle the same initial radius, draw 26 target radii from a power-law (Apollonian-like) distribution, for example sorted values proportional to k^(-0.5) for k = 1..n, rescaled so the total area is about 0.6 of the unit square, then shuffle them with the seed-derived rng. Place centres uniformly in the square with the radii as starting values. The rest of the restart (cap continuation, repair, selection by sum of radii) stays the same. This gives the local solver a starting point with a realistic spread of sizes, where the current start is uniform and small.
backlog.title: Power-law radius prior at initialisation

backlog.spec: For a random half of the restarts, seed the centres in concentric rings rather than uniformly. Put about 4 times sqrt(n) circles on the perimeter, spaced along the four sides with a random offset, and place the remaining circles on one or two inner rings or at random inside the inner square. Radii start at a small value. The rng decides the ring counts and offsets, so every seed explores a different layout. The other half of the restarts keep the current uniform start, so the diversity of the search is preserved.
backlog.title: Boundary-first ring seeding

backlog.spec: After the first restart, take the best packing found so far and apply each of the 8 symmetries of the square (identity, the 3 rotations, and 4 reflections, mapping centres by (x, y) to (x, y), (y, 1-x), (1-x, 1-y), (1-y, x), and the reflections). Run the radius-cap SLSQP continuation from each transformed copy with its radii as the start, then repair and keep the best. Those transforms give the same packing, so this step only helps if the local solver reaches a different basin from a slightly different start. Add small Gaussian jitter of scale 0.01 to the centres before the solve, using the seeded rng, to make the copies differ. Use this branch for about one quarter of the time budget and random restarts for the rest.
backlog.title: Dihedral-symmetry transforms of the incumbent as restarts

backlog.spec: During the early radius-cap stages (caps 0.05 to 0.2), replace the hard pair-overlap constraints with a smooth soft-minimum penalty. Define g_ij = dist_ij minus r_i minus r_j, and the constraint is -(1/beta) * log(sum over pairs of exp(-beta * g_ij)) >= 0 with beta increasing from 20 to 400 over the stages. Keep the exact hard pair constraints in the final stages (caps 0.24 onwards). The smooth version lets the optimiser move through overlapping configurations early on and gives a different basin structure. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged, including _repair.
backlog.title: Log-sum-exp soft pair constraints during early continuation

backlog.spec: Add a quadratic anchor term lambda * sum of ||c_i - c_i^seed||^2 to the SLSQP objective, where c^seed is the starting centre layout of that restart and lambda is 0.5 for the first half of the cap stages and 0 afterwards. The objective becomes minus sum(r) plus this anchor, so the early solve stays near its random start and the final stages are free to move. Tune nothing else. This acts as a regulariser that stops the early cap-continuation stages from jumping between basins, and it is a cheap change because it only adds a gradient term to the existing objective.
backlog.title: Anchored proximity regularisation during restarts

backlog.spec: Parametrise each radius as r_i = u_i^2 and optimise over u instead of r. Remove the r >= 0 inequality constraints from the SLSQP problem, since squares are nonnegative by construction, and keep the cap constraint as cap minus u_i^2 >= 0. Also replace the centre-box constraints by the bounds on c passed to SLSQP through its bounds argument, so they are not counted as inequality constraints. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. This changes the geometry of the search space and reduces the number of constraints the solver must handle at each iteration, so it may converge faster in the same time.
backlog.title: Squared-radius reparametrisation to drop nonnegativity constraints

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.92 of time_limit. Before each restart, estimate the duration of the previous restart as the maximum observed so far, and skip starting a new restart if the elapsed CPU time plus that estimate would exceed 0.95 of time_limit. This keeps every call well below the 45 s hard stop, which is 1.5 times the time limit, while using nearly all of the 30 s budget. The gain is a larger number of restarts within the same budget and no change to the search itself.
backlog.title: Use more of the CPU budget with a per-restart safety margin

backlog.spec: Along with the radius cap continuation, shrink the box that bounds centres. Start with centres bounded to [0.1, 0.9] in both coordinates for the first cap stage and expand the box linearly to [0, 1] by the last stage (the bounds passed to SLSQP through its bounds argument, not as constraints). This keeps the circles near the middle of the square early on, which reduces the number of boundary-stuck local optima, then lets them spread to the walls. Keep the cap continuation and _repair as they are.
backlog.title: Shrinking centre box as a continuation axis

backlog.spec: Keep a score for each of the start families (uniform random, power-law radius prior, ring seeding, and symmetry transforms of the incumbent). After each restart, update the family's score as an exponential moving average of the sum of radii it produced, relative to the best so far. Choose the family for the next restart with probability proportional to exp(score / 0.01), using the seeded rng, with a floor of 5 percent per family so that no family is starved. This lets the search allocate restarts to whichever start family currently yields the best packings, without fixing the mix in advance.
backlog.title: Weighted-restart bandit over initialisation families

backlog.spec: Replace the single SLSQP solve per restart with an alternating scheme. Fix the centres and solve the radii exactly as a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS): maximise sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, r_i <= wall distance, and r >= 0. Then fix the radii and take one SLSQP step over the centres only with those radii as the bound, which is a smooth problem in 2n variables. Repeat for about 6 rounds, or until the sum stops improving by more than 1e-9. Keep the existing cap continuation for the first SLSQP stage only. Keep the final _repair as a safety net.
backlog.title: Alternating LP-radii and SLSQP-centres

backlog.spec: Swap SLSQP for an augmented Lagrangian method in each restart. Minimise -sum(r) plus, for every constraint g(v) >= 0 (pair non-overlap, walls, r >= 0), a multiplier term (rho/2)*max(0, lambda/rho - g)^2 - lambda^2/(2 rho), using scipy.optimize.minimize with L-BFGS-B and analytic gradients. Update the multipliers lambda <- max(0, lambda - rho*g) and increase rho by a factor of 3 after each outer round, for about 12 outer rounds. Use the same random uniform start and cap continuation as before. Final SLSQP is optional. This makes each restart cheap and gives many more restarts within the time budget.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian with L-BFGS-B as the main solver

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centre initialisation with a scrambled Halton sequence in base 2 and 3 over [0.1, 0.9]^2, using the seed to draw a random digit permutation and a random offset for each restart. Add a small uniform jitter of about 0.02 to each point so the restarts still differ. Radii start at 0.05 as before. The even spread of the start reduces the chance of many clustered circles in one corner, so each SLSQP restart begins from a better-spread configuration. Nothing else in the solver changes.
backlog.title: Halton low-discrepancy starting points with jitter

backlog.spec: Track how many SLSQP restarts end with res.success true and how many hit the maxiter cap. Start with MAX_ITER=200 and ftol=1e-6. If the fraction hitting the cap is above 0.3, raise MAX_ITER by 50 for the next restart, up to 600. If the fraction is below 0.05, lower it by 25, down to 100. Also tighten the SLSQP ftol to 1e-9 for the final cap stage only. Stop the schedule when the time budget is used. This spends the budget where convergence is actually the bottleneck instead of using one fixed iteration limit everywhere.
backlog.title: Adaptive per-restart convergence budget

backlog.spec: In each restart, assign the 26 circles to K=3 radius classes with a random class sizes drawn from a Dirichlet prior. Optimise over centres and K class radii only, so the variable count drops from 3n to 2n+K. Constraints are written per pair using the class radius of each circle. After convergence, run one free SLSQP polish with all n radii starting from the tied solution. The tied stage explores a smaller and more structured space, and the free polish recovers the full optimum. Keep the existing cap continuation in the tied stage.
backlog.title: Radius-class tying for a reduced parametrisation

backlog.spec: Keep a list of the centres of all converged packings from previous restarts. For each new restart, add a penalty term to the SLSQP objective: lambda * sum over earlier packings and circles of exp(-||c_i - p_k||^2 / s^2), with s=0.15 and lambda decaying from 0.02 to 0 across the cap continuation stages. This pushes the search away from basins already found, so restarts cover more distinct basins. The penalty is zero in the final stage, so the returned packing is a true local optimum of the original problem. Keep the list capped at the last 20 packings.
backlog.title: Deflation repulsion from earlier optima

backlog.spec: After each restart's repaired packing is computed, build a signature: the sorted radii rounded to 2 decimals, plus the number of circles touching a wall rounded to the nearest integer. Store signatures in a set. If a new restart's signature matches an existing one, skip the rest of its continuation stages, since the same basin was already polished, and immediately start a fresh random restart. Count how many restarts are skipped and keep the best packing as before. This frees CPU time for new basins without changing the solver.
backlog.title: Basin deduplication with signature skipping

backlog.spec: In the first three cap stages, replace the SLSQP gradient of the objective with a smoothed version: average the gradient of -sum(r) over K=8 random perturbations of the centres, each drawn as Gaussian noise with sigma=0.01 times a scale that shrinks from 1 to 0 across the stages. Keep the constraint functions exact. The averaging smooths the landscape so the optimiser can cross small barriers between nearby basins. The later stages use the exact objective. Use the seed to make the noise reproducible.
backlog.title: Gaussian-smoothed objective for the early continuation

backlog.spec: Solve the dual form of the problem: for a fixed target total radius S, minimise the container side length L subject to sum(r) >= S, all circles inside [0, L]^2 and no overlaps. Start with L from the current best packing and S set to its sum. Use SLSQP over centres, radii, and L. After the solve, rescale the coordinates to the unit square by dividing by L, which keeps the packing valid. Repeat with S raised by 0.5 percent whenever the solve is feasible. This is a different route to the same optimum and can reach configurations the direct sum-maximisation misses.
backlog.title: Container-side shrinking with equal-sum target

backlog.spec: After the cap continuation finishes for a restart, identify rattlers as circles with fewer than 2 active contacts within 1e-6. Replace each rattler's centre with a new uniform random point inside the square, set its radius to 0.01, and run one more SLSQP stage over all variables with the same constraints. Keep the result only if the total radius sum improves. This tests whether the loose circles can find a better slot and costs one extra solve per restart. Keep the existing repair and return logic.
backlog.title: Two-pass refinement of each restart with a fresh random start for the rattlers

backlog.spec: In each _solve_once, draw a fixed weight w_i uniformly in [0.9, 1.1] per circle from rng. For every cap stage except the last, maximise sum(w_i * r_i) instead of sum(r_i). Run the final cap=1.0 stage with uniform weights so the returned objective is the true sum of radii. The weights break the symmetry of the early optima so different restarts land in different basins, without changing the final objective.
backlog.title: Per-circle random objective weights during continuation

backlog.spec: Run the first 10 restarts fully and record for each its pre-SLSQP features (initial mean nearest-neighbour distance, initial sum of pairwise distances, and the fraction of centres within 0.05 of a wall). Fit a ridge regression from these features to the final repaired radius sum. For later starts, generate candidate initial configurations (cheap, no SLSQP), predict their outcome with the surrogate, and run the full radius-cap SLSQP only on the top 30 percent of predictions. Refit the surrogate after each new full run. Keep the rest of solve unchanged.
backlog.title: Surrogate-filtered polishing of restarts

backlog.spec: Add a start family that places 26 circles on a 5x5 grid with one extra point, or on a 6x5 grid with 4 points removed, chosen at random from seed. Scale the grid to fill [0.1, 0.9], add uniform jitter of amplitude 0.05 to every centre, and set initial radii to 0.05. Use this start for half the restarts and the existing uniform start for the rest. This is a different lattice from the hexagonal start, and the defects give the continuation a broken symmetry to relax.
backlog.title: Square-grid-with-defects initialisation

backlog.spec: After each radius-cap SLSQP stage, add Gaussian noise to the centres with standard deviation 0.02 times the current cap divided by 0.4, then clip to [0,1]. Run the next stage from the jittered point. The noise shrinks as the cap grows, so early stages explore and late stages refine. Keep the best final repaired packing across restarts as before.
backlog.title: Centre jitter between continuation stages

backlog.spec: Replace the radius variables r with s, where r = exp(s), and optimise over s. This removes the r >= 0 constraint from the SLSQP constraint vector and keeps radii positive throughout. Map back with exp(s) before the cap constraints and repair step, and adjust the Jacobian-free constraints accordingly. The cap and wall constraints stay in terms of r. Initial s is log(INIT_RADIUS) for all circles.
backlog.title: Log-radius reparametrisation

backlog.spec: For each restart, split the 26 circles at random into four groups by assigning them to quadrants of the unit square using their random starting centres. Solve each quadrant as a separate packing inside its own square with the radius-cap SLSQP, then rescale the four local solutions into their quadrants and use the merged configuration as the start for one global radius-cap SLSQP run. This is a coarse-to-fine move that builds the layout from local blocks rather than a single random start.
backlog.title: Quadrant decomposition and global merge

backlog.spec: Precompute the pair index arrays (iu, and the squared-distance buffers) once per call to solve rather than inside each _solve_once, and compute the constraint vector with in-place operations on preallocated arrays. In _repair, replace the full n-by-n distance matrix recomputation at each of 50 iterations with a single recomputation followed by updates to the two changed rows. The search logic is unchanged; the goal is more restarts in the same 24 seconds of CPU time.
backlog.title: Cached index arrays and buffers for the inner loop

backlog.spec: During all radius-cap stages except the last, add a penalty lambda * sum over pairs of 1 / (d_ij^2 + eps) to the minimised objective, with eps = 1e-4 and lambda decaying geometrically from 0.01 at cap 0.05 to 0 at cap 0.4. The objective therefore pushes centres apart early and vanishes before the final cap=1.0 stage. Use the analytic gradient with respect to the centres so the cost stays low, and keep the radius-sum constraints as they are.
backlog.title: Coulomb repulsion regulariser annealed to zero

backlog.spec: Add a small quadratic term beta * sum_i ||c_i - (0.5, 0.5)||^2 to the minimised objective during the early cap stages, with beta = 0.02 decaying linearly to zero over the first half of the cap schedule. This biases the continuation toward compact layouts where radii can grow in the middle, and leaves the feasible set untouched. Final stages use the true objective, so the returned packing is optimal for the unregularised problem.
backlog.title: Centroid-pull regulariser on centres

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP restart, generate 64 random starts as a single numpy array and compute, in one vectorised pass, the minimum pairwise gap and the sum of feasible radii that a greedy radius assignment gives for each start. Only the best 4 starts by this score go through the full radius-cap SLSQP. Keep the time check and the repair step unchanged. This batches the cheap screening work across starts so most CPU time goes to the few candidates that look promising.
backlog.title: Cheap batch-vectorised screening of initial configurations

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random start in each restart with a greedy hole-filling build. Start from 3 random centres. Repeatedly compute the Delaunay triangulation of the current centres plus four mirror-free wall sentinels, take the circumcentre of each triangle with the largest distance to its nearest existing centre or wall, and place the next circle there with radius equal to that distance (clipped to the square). Stop at n=26 and use the resulting centres and radii as the start of the existing radius-cap SLSQP continuation. Randomise the choice among the top 3 holes using rng so that restarts differ.
backlog.title: Delaunay hole-filling initialisation

backlog.spec: Before the circle SLSQP, solve a relaxed problem in which every circle is an axis-aligned square of half-side r_i. Maximise sum r_i subject to the square-square non-overlap written as max(|x_i-x_j|, |y_i-y_j|) >= r_i + r_j, handled smoothly by requiring either the x or the y separation, with a random sign-pattern choice per pair seeded by rng, and the box constraints r_i <= x_i <= 1 - r_i. Use the resulting centres (and radii scaled to be feasible) as the starting point of the usual circle continuation. This gives a different contact topology from uniform random starts while keeping the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Chebyshev square-relaxation start

backlog.spec: After each restart's SLSQP converges, identify rattlers as circles with no active contact (gap below 1e-6 to any other circle or wall). Remove them and re-optimise only the rigid core (fewer variables, same cap continuation finished at cap 1.0). Then reinsert each rattler at the point of largest empty clearance found by a grid search over the square, with radius equal to that clearance clipped at 0, and run one short SLSQP over all circles starting from that configuration. Keep whichever packing has the larger sum of radii. This explicitly handles the loose circles that the current pipeline wastes budget on.
backlog.title: Rattler-core reduction and reinsertion

backlog.spec: Add a term -eps_k * (a . c) to the SLSQP objective, where a is a random unit vector per restart drawn from rng, c is the flattened centre vector, and eps_k decays geometrically from 0.05 to 0 across the cap-continuation stages, so the last stage is the unmodified sum-of-radii problem. The tilt breaks the symmetry of the uniform start and pushes the early stages toward distinct basins without changing the final objective. Keep the Jacobian of the tilt term analytic and the rest of the code unchanged.
backlog.title: Annealed random tilt of the objective

backlog.spec: Remove label symmetry from the search space by adding linear constraints r_0 >= r_1 >= ... >= r_{n-1} to the SLSQP problem in the final cap-continuation stages only (cap >= 0.2). Before solving, sort the initial radii descending and the initial centres in the same order. This shrinks the set of equivalent optima the local solver can wander between and removes the permutation redundancy from the feasible set. Verify the final packing still satisfies the non-overlap check after repair.
backlog.title: Radius-ordering symmetry breaking

backlog.spec: For the first 25 percent of each call's time budget, run scipy differential_evolution over the 26 centres only (52 variables, bounds in [0,1]). The objective is the negative sum of radii computed greedily as the largest radii consistent with the centres (r_i = min of wall clearances and half the nearest-neighbour distances) minus a 100 times squared-overlap penalty, with popsize 15 and maxiter capped so the stage stops by its time budget. Then pass the best population member through the existing cap-continuation SLSQP and repair. Use seed-derived rng for DE so results are reproducible.
backlog.title: Global differential evolution on a smooth penalty

backlog.spec: Extend the radius-cap continuation so that after each cap stage a short free SLSQP stage runs with the cap removed but the radii bounded by the previous cap plus 0.02. Alternate capped and free stages: capped at 0.05, free, capped at 0.07, free, and so on up to 0.4, then one final uncapped stage. The free stages let circles that were held back by the cap move again, while the cap keeps the early geometry coherent. Limit each free stage to 30 SLSQP iterations.
backlog.title: Two-sided cap continuation with free stages

backlog.spec: Wrap each SLSQP call with a callback that records the objective after every iteration. If the objective has improved by less than 1e-6 over the last 15 iterations and the constraint violation is below 1e-4, raise a private StopEarly exception caught around the minimize call and keep the last feasible iterate. This cuts time spent on converged-but-slow restarts, freeing the budget for more starts. Keep the MAX_ITER cap as an upper bound and make sure the final returned packing is still repaired before comparison.
backlog.title: Stall-triggered early abort of SLSQP

backlog.spec: After random initial centres are drawn, run 20 iterations of a weighted Lloyd relaxation in which each centre moves to the centroid of its power-diagram cell inside the unit square, where the cell weight for circle i is its initial radius squared. Estimate cell centroids by a fixed 200 by 200 grid of sample points assigned to the nearest weighted centre with (||x - c_j||^2 - r_j^2) as the power distance. Then pass the relaxed centres to the existing SLSQP continuation. This spreads the start more evenly than uniform random points without the greedy structure of max-min initialisation.
backlog.title: Power-diagram Lloyd relaxation of centres

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, identify active contacts with gap below 1e-7. Solve the KKT system for the active set with a single Gauss-Newton step on the equality constraints (contact gaps equal zero, boundary contacts equal zero) using numpy.linalg.lstsq, keeping only steps that increase sum of radii and keep all inactive gaps nonnegative, with a backtracking line search of at most 8 halvings. Repair afterwards with the existing function. This is a cheap final polish that does not require another SLSQP call and can recover the last 1e-6 of radius sum.
backlog.title: Bounded Newton-free polish of the incumbent via Lagrange multipliers

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centre start in some restarts with a greedy build. Shuffle the 26 indices with the seeded rng. For each circle in turn, evaluate a fixed grid of about 2000 candidate centres in [0,1]^2 (drawn from rng). For each candidate, the largest feasible radius is min(distance to each wall, distance to each placed centre minus its radius). Place the circle at the candidate with the largest feasible radius, and set its radius to that value times 0.9. The resulting centres and radii are the start for the usual SLSQP cap continuation. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Sequential Apollonius-style greedy construction as a start

backlog.spec: Each solve call first runs a vectorised numpy population of 64 starts at once. Each start has centres in [0,1]^2 and radii set to zero. Run about 300 steps of projected gradient ascent on the radius sum with a quadratic overlap penalty whose weight grows geometrically. Use numpy broadcasting over the population dimension, so each step costs one batched pairwise computation. Take the top 3 configurations by repaired radius sum, and run the existing SLSQP cap continuation only on those. Keep the time-budget loop, with the population stage counted inside TIME_FRACTION.
backlog.title: Batched projected-gradient population before SLSQP

backlog.spec: For a random subset of restarts, build the start as horizontal rows. Draw the number of rows from {4,5,6} and split the 26 circles into row counts that sum to 26, each row count drawn by rng between 3 and 7. Place the circles in each row evenly spaced across [0.1, 0.9], with the row heights evenly spaced and a random horizontal offset per row of up to half a spacing. Add uniform noise of 0.02 to every coordinate, clip to the box, and use these as the centre start with INIT_RADIUS. Then run the usual continuation. Alternate row and column orientation at random.
backlog.title: Random row-layout starts with per-row counts

backlog.spec: Instead of the fixed cap list from 0.05 to 0.4 in steps of 0.02 followed by 1.0, draw each restart's schedule from a small prior. Draw the starting cap uniformly from [0.03, 0.12], the final intermediate cap from [0.25, 0.5], and the number of intermediate steps from {8, 12, 16, 20}, all with the seeded rng. Use np.linspace between them and finish with cap 1.0. This tests whether a per-restart schedule diversifies the basins reached, with no change to the solver or to the repair step.
backlog.title: Randomised cap-continuation schedule per restart

backlog.spec: On a random third of the restarts, place four circles at the corners of the square, with centres at (r, r), (1-r, r), (r, 1-r), (1-r, 1-r) where r is drawn uniformly from [0.05, 0.2]. Give each of these four circles an initial radius equal to r. Place the remaining 22 centres uniformly in [0.1, 0.9]^2 as before. The corner circles are free variables for SLSQP and are not held fixed, so the continuation can move them. Keep the rest of the restart procedure unchanged.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored starts with random sizes

backlog.spec: Add an alternative local solver for some restarts. Fix a target T for the radius sum, starting at the incumbent's sum times 1.0 from the first best packing found. Solve the feasibility problem: minimise the sum of squared centre-pair overlaps plus squared wall violations, subject to sum(r) >= T and the cap constraints, with SLSQP. If the solver reports success, raise T by 0.002 and repeat from the solution. If it fails, lower T by 0.001. Stop when the step is below 0.0005 or the time slice is used. Pass the best feasible packing through the existing repair step.
backlog.title: Feasibility-form SLSQP with a sum constraint

backlog.spec: Rescale the SLSQP variables so every entry is of order one at the start of each continuation stage. Use centres divided by the current cap and radii divided by the current cap, with the cap taken from the stage. Divide every constraint by the current cap as well. Map the solution back to the original coordinates after each stage before the next stage starts. This does not change the feasible set, but it can change the conditioning seen by SLSQP. Keep the analytic-free finite-difference Jacobians and the existing repair.
backlog.title: Scale-normalised SLSQP variables and constraints

backlog.spec: Add a global stage for a fraction of the time budget, using scipy.optimize.dual_annealing. The objective takes a flat vector of 52 centre coordinates and returns minus the sum of the repaired radii. Radii are obtained by a fast greedy assignment: each radius is the largest value that keeps the circle inside the square and does not overlap the already-set circles in index order. Use bounds [0.05, 0.95] for each coordinate, a seeded rng, and maxiter set so the stage uses at most about 40 percent of the CPU budget. Then polish the best centres with the existing SLSQP cap continuation.
backlog.title: Dual annealing over centres with SLSQP local refinement

backlog.spec: On a random half of the restarts, generate the centre start with a dart-throwing Poisson-disk sampler on [0.05, 0.95]^2 using the seeded rng. Use a minimum spacing that starts at 0.2 and is reduced by a factor of 0.97 whenever 2000 attempts fail, until 26 points are placed. This gives an evenly spread start with a different structure from uniform noise. Assign each point the radius INIT_RADIUS and run the usual continuation. Keep the rest of the restart procedure and the repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Poisson-disk cell-seeded starts

backlog.spec: On every fourth restart, take the best packing found so far in this solve call and apply one of the eight symmetries of the square chosen at random by the seeded rng: identity, the three rotations, and the four reflections. Apply the transform to the centres, keep the radii, add Gaussian noise of 0.01 to the centres, clip to the box, and use the result as the start for the cap continuation from cap 0.05 onward, with the radii taken from the transformed incumbent. This reuses structure of the good packing while letting the continuation move every circle.
backlog.title: Random dihedral image of the incumbent as a restart seed

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP restart, discretise the unit square into a 40x40 grid of candidate centres. Place 26 circles on distinct cells with a tabu search: at each step, move one circle to a random nearby empty cell or swap two cells, score a layout by the sum over circles of the distance to the nearest other circle or wall (min-gap proxy), and keep a tabu list of the last 30 moves to avoid cycling. Run about 300 tabu steps from a random layout, take the best layout as the centre start for SLSQP, and use the cap-continuation schedule from the incumbent. Use the seed for all randomness. This replaces the uniform random centre start in a random half of the restarts.
backlog.title: Tabu search on a discrete occupancy grid, then SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random start with a short damped particle simulation. Place 26 particles at random in the square with random small velocities. Each step, apply a soft repulsive force from pairwise overlaps (linear spring on max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)) and a wall spring, add a viscous damping term and a small thermostat kick from the seeded RNG, and grow all radii slowly toward a target of about 0.1 per step, capped at 0.2. Run about 400 steps with numpy vectorised pair forces, then pass the centres and radii to the existing SLSQP cap continuation. Keep the cost per restart small so that many restarts fit in the budget.
backlog.title: Damped molecular-dynamics inflation as a start

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP local solver in each restart with an alternating-projection scheme. Keep radii and centres as variables. Each iteration performs one gradient-free step that increases the radii by a fixed fraction of the current slack, then projects the configuration back onto the non-overlap set by pushing each overlapping pair apart along its connecting line by half the overlap, and clamps centres and radii to the box. Stop when the maximum overlap is below 1e-9 or after 2000 iterations, then run one short SLSQP call with a tiny iteration cap to recover the exact local optimum. This is a projection method with no Lagrange multipliers, so it is a different local-search family from the SLSQP-only pipeline.
backlog.title: Alternating projections (POCS) instead of SLSQP for the feasible set

backlog.spec: Keep the cap-continuation schedule but make the SLSQP tolerance part of it. Use a loose ftol of 1e-3 and a maximum of 40 iterations for the early caps (0.05 to 0.2), then ftol 1e-6 and 120 iterations for the middle caps, and ftol 1e-12 with the full MAX_ITER for the final cap of 1.0. The intent is to spend less CPU on early stages that only move circles into the right basin, so that more restarts fit into the 80 percent budget, while the final stage still converges tightly. Keep everything else identical to the incumbent, including the repair step.
backlog.title: Tolerance annealing across the continuation

backlog.spec: On roughly half of the restarts after the first, take the best packing so far and apply a random affine strain to the centres: multiply the centre coordinates by a random 2x2 matrix with entries drawn from N(0, 0.03) added to the identity, re-centre on (0.5, 0.5), and clip to [0.02, 0.98]. Set the radii to 0.8 times their incumbent values, then run the existing radius-cap SLSQP continuation from this start, but with the first cap set to the incumbent's largest radius. Keep the best result by sum of radii after repair. This is a global shear-and-relax move rather than a per-circle jitter, so it can shift contact networks that single-circle perturbations do not reach.
backlog.title: Affine-strain shake of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Maintain a small archive of the centres of the best 10 distinct packings found so far. For each new restart after the first five, draw the start from a fitted isotropic Gaussian mixture: pick one archived packing at random, take its centre set, and add N(0, 0.05) jitter to every centre with a 0.2 probability of replacing one centre by a uniform random point. Clip to [0.05, 0.95] and assign radii of 0.05. Use only numpy and the seed. This turns the elite pool into a sampling density over starts instead of a list of parents for crossover, so the search concentrates on regions that already produced good sums.
backlog.title: Gaussian-mixture sampling of starts from the elite centres

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP call in each restart with scipy.optimize.least_squares using method 'trf'. Variables are the centres and radii. The residual vector contains max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij) for all pairs i<j, max(0, r_i - x_i), max(0, r_i - y_i), max(0, x_i + r_i - 1), max(0, y_i + r_i - 1), plus a penalty of minus a weight times r_i that drives radii to grow. Use a weight that increases from 0.01 to 1 over three solves with the same start, and at the end run one SLSQP pass with a short iteration cap to clean up contacts. This keeps the local solver different from the current constrained optimiser while still using the same restart loop and repair step.
backlog.title: Least-squares overlap residuals with trust-region reflective solver

backlog.spec: Run the radius-cap continuation in the opposite direction. Start from a random uniform packing with caps of 1.0, then reduce the cap through 0.6, 0.4, 0.3, 0.25, 0.2, and 0.15 down to 0.1 and keep the final stage uncapped at 1.0 for polishing. The reversal lets the largest circles settle first and forces the small ones to fill the gaps, which is the opposite of the current small-to-large schedule. Keep the number of stages and iteration cap per stage similar to the incumbent. Select between the forward and reversed schedule by a coin flip from the seed, so both are represented across restarts.
backlog.title: Reversed cap continuation from large to small

backlog.spec: After each restart's final SLSQP stage, identify the rigid core as the circles with at least three contacts within 1e-6 of tangency. For the next restart derived from the incumbent, freeze the centres and radii of the rigid core, re-randomise the centres and radii of the remaining rattlers and boundary-free circles uniformly in the square with radii 0.05, and re-run the radius-cap continuation with the core fixed as equality constraints for the first two stages. Then release the core and run the full continuation. Repeat this with a fresh random seed for the freed circles. This is a partial restart that keeps good structure while reopening the loose parts, which is different from a global perturbation.
backlog.title: Freeze-and-thaw of the rigid core

backlog.spec: Give each restart a random rectangle of aspect ratio drawn log-uniformly from [0.8, 1.25], with width w and height h such that w times h equals 1. Place the initial centres uniformly inside this rectangle and run the radius-cap SLSQP continuation with the box constraints of the rectangle. Then, in a final stage, morph the box to the unit square by linearly interpolating the box bounds over five SLSQP solves, using the previous solution as the start each time. The final stage must satisfy the exact unit square bounds, so the repair step still applies. This is a container-side continuation that lets the packing reorganise through non-square intermediate shapes.
backlog.title: Random aspect-ratio start that anneals to the square

backlog.spec: After SLSQP and before the repair step, run a cheap exact inflation pass. Repeat up to 20 sweeps: for each circle i in random order, set r_i to the largest value allowed by the walls (min of c_i and 1 - c_i over both coordinates) and by every neighbour j (d_ij - r_j). Take the minimum of these bounds, never decreasing r_i. Stop when the total sum gains less than 1e-12. Keep the existing _repair as the final safety net, so the output stays valid. This recovers the radius slack that SLSQP leaves through its constraint tolerance, at O(n^2) per sweep.
backlog.title: Exact greedy inflation polish after each SLSQP restart

backlog.spec: Keep the 5 best distinct packings found so far. For each one, sort its circles by radius, then align every packing to the best one with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on the squared centre distances, with the 8 dihedral symmetries of the square tried as alternatives. Average the aligned centres and radii over the elite set to form a consensus packing. Use this consensus, with small Gaussian jitter (sigma 0.02), as the start of every second restart after the first 20. The rest of the pipeline is unchanged. This exploits structure that is shared across basins without a crossover operator.
backlog.title: Hungarian-matched consensus seed from the elite packings

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP restart, run a small parallel-tempering pool of 6 replicas of the 26 centres in the unit square. Each replica minimises the energy E = sum over pairs of max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2 plus wall overlaps, with radii fixed at a common value that is slowly raised. Use a temperature ladder from 1e-4 to 1e-2 geometric. Each sweep does Metropolis moves of size 0.05 times the replica's temperature rank, followed by swap attempts between neighbouring temperatures every 10 sweeps. Run for a fixed budget of 300 sweeps and feed the lowest-energy replica's centres into SLSQP. This gives an annealed, physically motivated start instead of a uniform draw.
backlog.title: Parallel-tempering start generator on overlap energy

backlog.spec: Run the first 25 restarts as usual and record, for each, a feature vector computed from its random start (mean nearest-neighbour distance, number of starts within 0.1 of a wall, the variance of the centres, and the fraction of starts in the central quarter). Fit a ridge regression with lambda 1.0 from these features to the final sum of radii. For the remaining restarts, draw 20 candidate starts for each slot, score them with the fitted model, and run SLSQP only on the top-scoring candidate. Refit after every 10 new restarts, using all data so far. The score only chooses which random start to use. It never changes the optimiser or the constraints.
backlog.title: Learned start scoring by ridge regression

backlog.spec: On each restart, first solve a 13-circle packing with the existing radius-cap SLSQP continuation, using 2 fewer continuation stages to save time. Then split every circle into two daughters. Each daughter's centre is the parent centre shifted by plus or minus 0.5 r along a random direction, and its radius is 0.5 r times a uniform factor in [0.8, 1.0]. Keep the 26 best daughters by radius if the split yields more than 26, and pad with random small circles if fewer. Then run the normal full continuation SLSQP on the 26 circles. This coarse-to-fine construction is a different architecture from the uniform start and may place the large circles correctly before the fine structure forms.
backlog.title: Coarse-to-fine split from a 13-circle packing

backlog.spec: After the first 40 restarts, take the incumbent and its SLSQP constraint multipliers from the last solve, which scipy returns as res.jac for the active set (the multiplier of constraint k is estimated from the gradient of the objective against the active constraint Jacobians with a least-squares solve). Rank circles by the sum of multipliers of their active contacts. Re-randomise the centres of the 3 circles with the smallest sum, which are the least constrained, to uniform positions in [0.1, 0.9]^2. Keep all other circles fixed at their incumbent positions, then run the normal continuation SLSQP with a cap starting at the incumbent's smallest radius. Accept the result only if it beats the incumbent.
backlog.title: Dual-multiplier-guided perturbation of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centres in each restart with a short growth simulation. Start 26 points at random positions with radius 0.01. Repeat 400 steps: give each circle a random displacement of size 0.02 times a shrinking step factor, reject any displacement that creates an overlap, then grow every radius by a factor of 1.002 up to the largest value that keeps the packing feasible given the current neighbours. Use the resulting centres and radii as the start of the SLSQP continuation. Use the seed to make the random moves reproducible. The step factor halves every 100 steps, so the growth finishes in a near-jammed state.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger style growth as a start

backlog.spec: Add a regulariser to the SLSQP objective, minus sum(r) plus lambda times the variance of r, with lambda starting at 0.05 and multiplied by 0.7 at each cap-continuation stage until it is below 1e-4. At the final stage, set lambda to zero and run one unregularised SLSQP solve to recover the true sum. The variance term pushes the solver to explore packings with uneven radius classes, which the plain sum objective often misses. Apply the regulariser on each restart independently, so no state carries over. Keep the constraints and the repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Annealed radius-variance regulariser

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform draw of the centres with a draw from a product of Beta distributions. For each restart, pick a shape pair (a, b) from a seeded set of values {(0.7, 0.7), (1.0, 1.0), (1.5, 1.5), (2.0, 2.0)}, then draw each centre coordinate from Beta(a, b) and map it into [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. The shapes (a, b) below 1 push circles to the walls and shapes above 1 push them to the middle. Choose the shape at random per restart, so the search covers both wall-heavy and centre-heavy starts. The rest of the pipeline stays as it is.
backlog.title: Beta-distributed centre density for the random start

backlog.spec: At the start of solve, draw a pool of 200 random centre sets with the seed, and score each one by a fast penalty energy, the sum of squared pair overlaps at a fixed radius of 0.09, computed in a single vectorised numpy call on the stacked (200, 26, 2) array. Sort the pool by energy and run the full SLSQP continuation on the 40 lowest-energy starts in order, until the time budget is used. Replace the random uniform draw in the restart loop with this pool. The batch scoring costs a few milliseconds and needs no extra solver, and it gives the continuation a better-ordered set of starts.
backlog.title: Two-stage multi-start with a shared starting pool of 200 centres

backlog.spec: Each call, after the first restart, generate 400 candidate perturbations of the best packing's centres (Gaussian noise with a random scale in [0.005, 0.1] per candidate). Score every candidate in one batched numpy pass with a cheap feasible-radius proxy: start from r_i = min(wall distance), then 5 vectorised fixed-point sweeps of r_i = min(r_i, min_j (d_ij - r_j)) over the batch, and sum the radii. Run SLSQP (the existing cap continuation) only on the top 3 candidates and keep the best result. Leave the random restarts unchanged for the other part of the budget.
backlog.title: Vectorised perturbation screen of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP restart, replace the uniform random centres with a maximin-spread configuration: solve max t subject to |c_i - c_j|^2 >= t and wall margins >= 0.05, using SLSQP over the 2n centre coordinates plus t, started from a random layout, with 100 iterations. Use the resulting centres as the start for the usual radius-cap continuation, with radii initialised to 0.5 times the distance to the nearest neighbour. Only the start changes; the rest of the restart is identical.
backlog.title: Maximin-spread centre start

backlog.spec: After each restart converges, find the largest empty circle: evaluate a 300 by 300 grid over the square, compute the distance to the nearest centre minus its radius, and take the grid point with the largest free clearance. Move the circle with the smallest Lagrange-multiplier-weighted contact load (or the smallest radius if multipliers are unavailable) to that point, set its radius to the clearance, and rerun the radius-cap SLSQP continuation from the new configuration. Keep the move only if the total radius sum rises. Apply this at most three times per restart.
backlog.title: Largest-hole hopping on converged packings

backlog.spec: Give SLSQP restart k a maxiter budget of 40 times the k-th term of the Luby sequence (1,1,2,1,1,2,4,1,...), capped at 400, instead of the fixed MAX_ITER of 200 for every stage. Keep the same cap-continuation stages. The schedule is fixed by index, so no performance feedback is used. This gives many cheap short runs with occasional long ones, which tests whether the best basin is reached more often under a mixed-length budget.
backlog.title: Luby-sequence iteration budget per restart

backlog.spec: Remove the rigid-motion freedom from the parametrisation. In each SLSQP restart, fix the largest initial circle at the corner (r, r) and remove its two centre coordinates from the decision vector. Pass the reduced vector to SLSQP and rebuild the full centres before the repair step. Keep all constraints and the cap continuation as they are. This is a one-off dimension cut that is simple to implement and changes only the variable layout.
backlog.title: Gauge-fixed coordinates

backlog.spec: After the restarts finish, take the best packing and run a simultaneous-perturbation stochastic approximation loop for the last 10 percent of the budget. Each iteration draws a random +-1 direction for all centre and radius coordinates, evaluates a penalised score (sum of radii minus 50 times the total pair and wall overlap), and updates the variables with gains a_k = 0.01/(k+1)^0.6 and c_k = 0.002/(k+1)^0.1. Keep the best feasible state seen, and finish with the existing repair step. This is a derivative-free bold polish that does not share SLSQP's active-set behaviour.
backlog.title: SPSA polish of the best packing

backlog.spec: After each restart's global SLSQP stage, repeat 6 times: choose a random subset of 8 circles, fix all other centres and radii, and run SLSQP over only the subset's centres and radii with the full constraint set (fixed circles appear as constants). Accept the block update only if the total radius sum rises, then finish with one full SLSQP pass. This decomposes the problem into small local solves that can escape configurations a global solve cannot leave.
backlog.title: Block-coordinate SLSQP on random subsets

backlog.spec: On half of the restarts, place the 26 initial centres on a sunflower (Vogel) spiral: point k sits at radius sqrt((k+0.5)/n) and angle k times the golden angle plus a random offset, mapped to the square by scaling into [0.1, 0.9]^2 with a random shear of up to 0.1. Keep the other half of the restarts on the uniform random start. Radii start at 0.05 as before. This is a new data-initialisation family, with the spiral covering the square quasi-uniformly.
backlog.title: Vogel-spiral sunflower start

backlog.spec: During the first two cap-continuation stages of each restart, add to the SLSQP objective a soft wall penalty of the form 0.02 times the sum of exp(-(distance to wall minus radius)/0.02) over all circles and four walls, with an analytic gradient. Linearly reduce the coefficient to zero over those two stages so the final stages optimise the true sum of radii. This regulariser acts only on the container edges, unlike the pair Coulomb penalty already tried.
backlog.title: Soft container-wall repulsion annealed to zero

backlog.spec: Re-parametrise each centre as (0.5 + rho cos(theta), 0.5 + rho sin(theta)) with rho in [0, 0.71] and theta free, with the square enforced by the existing wall constraints. The SLSQP decision vector holds (rho_i, theta_i, r_i) for each circle. Initialise rho uniformly in [0, 0.5] and theta uniformly in [0, 2 pi). Pass analytic gradients through the chain rule. Repair and final output are unchanged. This is an architecture change that alters the geometry of the search space, not the constraints.
backlog.title: Polar parametrisation of centres

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP restart, relax the 26 centres on a unit torus: minimise a soft overlap energy where distances use the minimum-image convention, so there are no walls. Use a short L-BFGS-B run from the uniform random start with a seeded RNG. Then map the torus configuration into [0,1]^2 by a random translation and a rescale toward the centre so that the wall terms are satisfied, and hand that start to the existing radius-cap SLSQP continuation. The torus removes boundary effects, so the start tends to a bulk-like lattice pattern. Keep the repair step as is.
backlog.title: Torus-relaxed start

backlog.spec: Treat the energy of a centre set as minus the optimal sum of radii, where the radii come from a fast LP (HiGHS linprog) with the pair and wall constraints. Run a short overdamped Langevin walk on the centres with Gaussian steps whose scale decays geometrically over the iterations, accepting moves by Metropolis with a temperature that also decays. Keep the best feasible centre set seen. Run SLSQP once on that best set at the end of the walk. The walk is a global search over the centre landscape, independent of SLSQP's local basin.
backlog.title: Langevin sampling of centres with LP-optimal radii as energy

backlog.spec: Split the restart budget across four islands, each with its own fixed radius-cap schedule (for example one coarse, one fine, one with an extra free stage, one with a geometric grid). Each island keeps its own best packing. Every fixed number of restarts, copy the best packing of one island into the start pool of another, chosen at random with a seeded RNG, and use it as a warm start for one restart. Return the overall best packing, repaired as before. The islands keep the search diverse while migration spreads good basins.
backlog.title: Island model with elite migration

backlog.spec: Within each restart, the cap-continuation stages produce a sequence of solution vectors x_k. After at least three stages, apply Anderson acceleration (depth 2, with least-squares mixing of the last residuals) to the vector of centres and radii to form a candidate start for the next stage. Accept the candidate only if its sum of radii is no worse than the plain SLSQP result, otherwise use the plain iterate. This is a cheap extrapolation between stages that may land in better basins, and it adds no new solver.
backlog.title: Anderson-mixed iterates across cap stages

backlog.spec: For each start, compute the Voronoi diagram of the initial centres, clipped to the unit square (use a dense grid of 200 by 200 points to find each cell's nearest-site membership). Set each circle's radius cap in the cap-continuation to half its cell's approximate inradius, that is the distance from the centre to the farthest point of its cell, times a factor of 0.9. Use these per-circle caps instead of the uniform cap in the early stages, and switch to the uniform schedule for the last stage. The caps keep the early configuration spread out, so SLSQP does not collapse circles into one corner.
backlog.title: Voronoi-inradius per-circle radius caps

backlog.spec: Replace the arithmetic cap schedule (0.05 to 0.40 in steps of 0.02, then 1.0) with a geometric grid from 0.05 to 0.40 using a ratio of about 1.04, then 1.0. This spends more stages on small caps, where the early structure forms, and fewer on large caps. Keep the other settings unchanged. The change touches one line and a small count of stages, and it is a direct test of whether the cap spacing matters.
backlog.title: Geometric cap grid

backlog.spec: On a random half of the restarts, build the initial centres from a patch of a quasi-periodic tiling: take points from a 2D cut-and-project construction with a random irrational slope and offset, keep the 26 points nearest to the square centre, then rescale them to fill [0.1, 0.9]^2. Give the others the existing uniform random start. Jitter all centres by a small seeded Gaussian. Starts from a quasi-periodic order are non-lattice and can reach configurations that hexagonal and square starts miss.
backlog.title: Quasi-crystal patch start

backlog.spec: Re-parametrise the centres as barycentric combinations over a fixed fan of eight triangles that tile the unit square, with each triangle's corner positions chosen by the seed. A centre is then a convex combination of three triangle corners with softmax weights, so the box constraints hold by construction and the box constraints drop out of SLSQP. Only the pair and radius constraints stay, which shrinks the constraint count. The repair step still checks the final packing in double precision. The map is smooth, so the analytic gradient is a short chain rule.
backlog.title: Barycentric fan parametrisation

backlog.spec: In the last radius-cap stage, which uses the uniform cap of 1.0, add a small reward of 0.002 times the number of near-contact pairs (pairs with gap below 1e-3) to the objective. The reward is a smooth sigmoid of the gap, so it stays differentiable. The bonus favours rigid configurations with many contacts over loose ones with the same sum of radii. Drop the bonus in the final polish so that the reported sum of radii is the true objective. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Contact-count bonus in the final stage

backlog.spec: After the first restart, each later restart takes the best packing and removes its two smallest-radius circles. It then places each removed circle at the largest empty hole, found as the Voronoi vertex with the greatest distance to the nearest centre inside the unit square, and gives both circles a random radius at most 0.5 of that hole's distance. Run the usual radius-cap continuation on the resulting configuration. This is a targeted change to a near-optimal start, and it differs from random insertion by picking holes deterministically.
backlog.title: Two-scale hole-targeted restart

backlog.spec: After each restart's final SLSQP stage, form the Hessian of the Lagrangian (objective plus active-contact multipliers, taken from the SLSQP result or estimated by least squares on the KKT residual) over the centres and radii, restricted to the active set. If its smallest eigenvalue is negative, step along the corresponding eigenvector by a small amount (about 0.01) in both signs, re-run the radius-cap final stage from each perturbed point, and keep the best sum. Skip the step when no negative curvature is found, so the cost is one eigen-decomposition per restart.
backlog.title: Saddle escape via negative curvature of the Lagrangian

backlog.spec: Build the contact network of the incumbent (pairs with gap below 1e-6 plus wall contacts). Form the linearised stiffness matrix of the overlap energy over the 2n centre coordinates and take its lowest non-zero eigenvectors, which are the soft modes. For each new restart after the first, perturb the incumbent centres along a random combination of the 3 softest modes with amplitude drawn from [0.02, 0.06], clip to the box, then run the radius-cap continuation from the repaired perturbed packing. Keep the usual best-of-restarts rule.
backlog.title: Soft-mode kick along low vibrational modes

backlog.spec: On every other restart after the first, pick a random centre c0 in the square and a radius R in [0.2, 0.45]. Take all circles whose centres lie within R of c0 and rotate their centres about c0 by a random angle in [-30, 30] degrees, leaving the others fixed. Clip to the box, repair the radii, and run only the last two stages of the radius-cap continuation (caps 0.3 and 1.0) to re-settle. Keep the best packing by sum of radii.
backlog.title: Cluster rotation move on the incumbent

backlog.spec: After a restart converges, identify circles whose radius equals their distance to a wall within 1e-7. For each such circle, drop the wall-normal coordinate from the decision vector and fix it at r (or 1-r) so the reduced SLSQP has fewer variables and constraints. Run a short reduced SLSQP over the remaining free coordinates, then map back to full coordinates and run one normal full-space SLSQP stage to confirm feasibility. Accept the result only if its sum exceeds the pre-reduction sum.
backlog.title: Wall-contact coordinate elimination

backlog.spec: During the early radius-cap stages (caps 0.05 to 0.2), add a lower bound r_i >= 0.02 to the SLSQP box so that no circle collapses to zero and gets stuck as a rattler. Release the floor for the last two stages (caps 0.3 and 1.0). This keeps every circle in play while the centres are still reorganising, and it changes only bounds on the radii, not the objective or the pair constraints.
backlog.title: Radius-floor continuation

backlog.spec: Set the radius-cap continuation grid from the incumbent packing rather than a fixed 0.05 to 0.4 range. Take the 26 incumbent radii, compute their quantiles at 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9, and use these five values (plus 1.0 at the end) as cap stages, each restart perturbing them by a random factor in [0.9, 1.1] drawn from the seed. For the first restart use the default grid. This ties the continuation to the scale of the best solution found so far.
backlog.title: Incumbent-quantile cap grid

backlog.spec: Each restart solves a packing for 24 circles and one for 28 circles with the existing cap continuation. Take the 28-circle packing and remove the two circles of smallest radius (or the two whose removal leaves the best sum after one SLSQP polish). Take the 24-circle packing and insert two circles at the two largest holes found by a 200 by 200 grid search. Polish both candidates with the usual final SLSQP stage and keep the better one. This is a bolder ladder that brackets 26 from both sides.
backlog.title: Two-stage ladder from 24 and 28 optima

backlog.spec: Replace the constraint d_ij >= r_i + r_j in the cap continuation by d_ij >= (r_i + r_j)(1 + eps_k) where eps_k decreases geometrically from 0.02 at the first stage to 0 at the final stage. The margin keeps early stages strictly feasible with spare room for reorganisation, and it is removed before the last stage so the final packing is tight. Keep the repair step unchanged as the last safety net.
backlog.title: Pairwise margin annealing to zero

backlog.spec: Allocate each restart a CPU budget from a seeded log-uniform draw between 0.5 and 4 seconds, rather than running restarts to the end of their own schedule. A restart that exceeds its slice is cut off after the current stage and its best feasible iterate is repaired and scored. Restarts keep the full cap schedule, but the slice lets more restarts fit in the 80 percent window, and the slice is recorded so that the total stays inside TIME_FRACTION.
backlog.title: Per-restart seed-driven time slicing

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP restart, project the random start onto the approximate feasible set with 30 iterations of a batched Gauss-Newton step on the stacked pair and wall residuals, using a dense numpy normal-equation solve on the 2n-dimensional centre vector with radii fixed at 0.05. Vectorise the residuals over all pairs in one array op per iteration. Then hand the projected centres to the usual radius-cap continuation.
