This is a cheap, deterministic-in-seed alternative to the random uniform start that keeps the SLSQP stages unchanged.
backlog.title: Batched Gauss-Newton overlap projection

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centre start in half of the restarts with a max-min spreading stage. Solve SLSQP on variables (centres, t) to maximise t subject to |c_i - c_j|^2 >= t^2 for all pairs and t/2 <= c_i <= 1 - t/2 coordinate-wise, starting from a random layout. Then fix the centres and solve an exact LP with scipy linprog (HiGHS) for radii: maximise sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij, r_i <= x_i, r_i <= y_i, r_i <= 1 - x_i, r_i <= 1 - y_i, r >= 0. Feed the (centres, LP radii) pair into the existing radius-cap continuation. Keep the rest of solve() unchanged and seed all randomness from rng.
backlog.title: Spread-then-LP start generator

backlog.spec: For a random third of the restarts, build the initial centres as concentric rings about (0.5, 0.5). Draw a ring count K from {2, 3, 4}, split the 26 circles into rings with counts drawn at random summing to 26 (each ring at least 1), place ring k at radius proportional to k with a random global scale in [0.25, 0.4], and offset each ring by an independent random angle. Add Gaussian jitter of 0.01 to every coordinate and clip to [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. Pass the result to the existing radius-cap SLSQP continuation unchanged.
backlog.title: Concentric ring seeding around the square centre

backlog.spec: Keep the best 6 distinct packings found so far. For a restart after the first two, choose two parents at random from the pool. Draw a random line through the unit square, and take the circles of parent A on one side and parent B on the other. Count the circles on each side, then fix the total at 26 by deleting a random circle from the surplus side or inserting a random point in the largest gap on the deficit side. Use the spliced centres as the start for the radius-cap SLSQP continuation. Standard Deaven-Ho cut-and-splice: the crossover is a geometric cut, not a value blend.
backlog.title: Cut-and-splice crossover on the elite pool

backlog.spec: For a random subset of restarts, build a random geometric graph on the 26 nodes: connect each node to its k nearest nodes in a random 2-D Gaussian cloud, with k drawn from {3, 4, 5}. Compute the normalised graph Laplacian and take the two eigenvectors with the smallest non-trivial eigenvalues. Rescale each eigenvector coordinate to fit [0.1, 0.9] in the unit square, then add small Gaussian jitter. Use these as initial centres for the existing radius-cap SLSQP continuation. The graph gives a random topology that spreads the points out by spectral embedding, not by uniform sampling.
backlog.title: Laplacian eigenmap seeding

backlog.spec: For a random quarter of the restarts, build the start from 13 dimers plus one singleton. Each dimer is two centres placed at a random location with separation 2 * 0.05 along a random direction, and the singleton is placed at a random location. Draw the dimer centres uniformly on [0.1, 0.9]^2 and keep the offsets so that both members of a dimer lie inside the box. Give all 26 radii INIT_RADIUS and pass the start to the existing radius-cap SLSQP continuation. The dimers force a paired contact structure that uniform starts rarely produce.
backlog.title: Dimer-pair start

backlog.spec: After each restart's SLSQP continuation, keep the final centres fixed and sample 30 random positive weight vectors w drawn from a Dirichlet(1) distribution. For each w, solve an exact HiGHS LP maximising w . r subject to the same pair and wall constraints as in the repair LP, then compute the sum of the resulting radii. Keep the radii with the largest sum, which is a cheap check on whether the current centres admit a better radius assignment. Use these radii for the final packing of that restart. This replaces the greedy shrink repair and only reads the centres.
backlog.title: Random-weight LP radius sampler on fixed centres

backlog.spec: The radius-cap continuation currently rises to 0.4 and then 1.0. Set the ladder adaptively: after the first restart, record the best sum S. For later restarts, end the cap ladder at min(1.0, 0.6 * S / 26 * 3) and use a step of 0.02 up to that ceiling. Always end with a free stage at cap 1.0. This removes the wasted stages at caps well above the typical radius and gives the remaining stages more iterations. The code change is one line in the cap list and one stored value.
backlog.title: Cap-ceiling set from the running best

backlog.spec: Split the CPU budget into a 'scout' phase using the first 25 percent of TIME_FRACTION * time_limit and a 'deep' phase using the rest. In the scout phase run ordinary restarts with MAX_ITER set to 60. Then take the top 3 packings by sum and run each through the full cap continuation with MAX_ITER set to 200, using the remaining time, keeping the best. This is a deterministic two-speed schedule without bandit weights, and it differs from successive halving in that the survivors get an additional full continuation rather than a single extra stage.
backlog.title: Two-speed restart timing

backlog.spec: For a random third of the restarts, rotate the whole initial layout by a random angle theta in [0, pi/4] about (0.5, 0.5) before SLSQP, then clip the centres to [0, 1] and set radii to INIT_RADIUS. Because the square is not rotationally symmetric, the initial layout meets the walls at different angles, which changes which circles start in the corners. Leave the rest of the optimiser and the repair unchanged. This is a bounded-rotation variant of the dihedral transforms already tested, so it is not a copy of them.
backlog.title: Wall-side rotated restart frame

backlog.spec: For every fifth restart, start from the incumbent's centres and reset only a random subset of 8 circles to uniform random positions. Keep the other 18 centres and all radii from the incumbent, then run the radius-cap continuation with the cap starting at 0.12 instead of 0.05, since the kept circles already have large radii. Take the best packing over all restarts as before. This is a batch-level restart mix: the bulk of each start is the incumbent and the randomness is a local partial reset, which is different from the full-perturbation basin hopping already rejected.
backlog.title: Partial-update restarts from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Treat the radius-cap continuation parameters as a small vector: start cap in [0.02, 0.2], cap step in [0.005, 0.05], number of SLSQP iterations per stage in [50, 300], and a final-stage flag. Keep a list of (parameter vector, final sum of radii after repair) for every restart so far. After the first 8 restarts, fit a numpy-only Gaussian process (RBF kernel, length scale set to the median pairwise distance of the observed parameters, noise 1e-4) to these observations. For each new restart, draw 300 random candidate vectors, score them by expected improvement over the best observed sum, and run the restart with the best candidate. Everything is seeded from rng and stays inside the CPU-time loop.
backlog.title: GP-guided cap-schedule search

backlog.spec: Parametrise the random initial-centre distribution as a Beta(a, b) product over the square with per-axis parameters, plus a radius-start mean. Start with a=b=1 and the current radius start. Each generation, draw 20 starts, run the existing SLSQP cap continuation on each, and record the repaired sum. Refit a and b (and the radius mean) by moment matching to the top 25 percent of starts, with a small floor on the variance so the distribution never collapses to a point. Iterate generations until the time budget is spent, always keeping the overall best packing. All draws use rng from the seed.
backlog.title: Cross-entropy adaptation of start distributions

backlog.spec: Re-express the problem with the radius of each circle represented as the height of a cone over the square. Start from the current random centres and set each radius to its distance to the nearest container wall. Then run SLSQP on the same objective, but add the pairwise constraint d_ij >= r_i + r_j only for pairs whose centres are within 2.5 times the current mean radius, and recompute the pair set once per cap stage. This is a different constraint topology from the full pair set and from the sparse neighbour list, and it lets the search reshape the contact graph between stages. Keep the exact repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Cone-lifted circle formulation

backlog.spec: After the first restart, run a Metropolis chain on the best packing's contact graph. A move picks one active contact at random and removes it by slightly separating its two circles (a random displacement of about 0.02 along the contact normal). It then re-solves the cap continuation starting from a small number of SLSQP iterations (about 80) and accepts the new packing with probability min(1, exp((S_new - S_old)/T)). Set T to 0.002 and decay it geometrically to 0.0002 over the remaining budget. Keep the best packing seen. This explores neighbouring contact topologies rather than resampling centres from scratch.
backlog.title: Metropolis walk over contact graphs

backlog.spec: On each restart, generate the random centre layout for one of two mirrored frames: the standard frame, or the frame reflected across the diagonal x = y with a per-restart random choice. Run the full cap continuation in whichever frame is chosen, then map the result back to the standard frame by the inverse reflection. Both frames are equally likely, so the search covers the mirror-image basins with the same budget. Repair and the best-of selection stay exactly as they are, so the only change is the frame transform.
backlog.title: Sign-flip symmetric pair of restarts

backlog.spec: Keep the cap-continuation SLSQP unchanged except for the variables. Each centre coordinate is written as c = 0.5 + 0.5 * tanh(u) with unconstrained u in R, and each radius as r = s^2 with s in R, which removes the box and the nonnegativity constraints from the solver. The wall constraints become automatically satisfied by the parametrisation, and the cap constraint is kept on r. Pass analytic Jacobians for the transform chain. Run the same cap schedule and repair. The goal is to let SLSQP move freely near the walls without active-bound degeneracies.
backlog.title: Hyperbolic-tangent box reparametrisation

backlog.spec: Generate 40 random centre layouts per batch with the usual uniform start. For each layout, compute the radii by solving the LP that maximises the sum of radii subject to pairwise and wall constraints, using a single HiGHS linprog call on the fixed centres. Score each layout by its LP sum. Keep the top 3 layouts and run the full cap continuation SLSQP on those only. Repeat batches until 60 percent of the CPU budget is used, then spend the rest on the best-so-far continuation. This puts an exact cheap screen in front of the expensive solver.
backlog.title: Population restarts with batched LP radius scoring

backlog.spec: On every second restart after the first, build the start by taking the current best packing's radius profile, sorting it, and assigning the sorted values to a fresh random permutation of the centres. Multiply each radius by a factor exp(0.3 * z) with z standard normal, clipped to a range of 0.5 to 1.5. Keep centres uniform on [0.1, 0.9] as in the original start. Then run the cap continuation and repair as usual. This keeps the size statistics of the best packing while randomising the geometry, which is a different start family from the previous ones tried.
backlog.title: Noise-scaled restarts from the incumbent's radius profile

backlog.spec: Add a small regularisation term to the cap-continuation SLSQP objective: minus the sum of radii plus lambda times the variance of the radii, with lambda set to 0.02 during the first half of the cap schedule and 0 afterwards. The variance term discourages early freezing of one large circle and a crowd of tiny ones, which tends to trap SLSQP. Analytic gradient is simple: the derivative of the variance with respect to each radius is 2 (r_i - mean) / n. Keep the constraints, repair, and best-of selection unchanged.
backlog.title: Gauge-normalised objective with a radius-ratio penalty

backlog.spec: Replace the monotone cap sweep with a bisection over a target total radius. Start with a target of 2.60. For each target, run SLSQP in feasibility form: minimise the sum of squared constraint violations of d_ij >= r_i + r_j, the walls, and sum r >= target, starting from the last successful solution (or the random start on the first step). If the violation falls below 1e-9, raise the target by half the current step, otherwise lower it. Stop when the step is below 0.001 and run repair on the final feasible packing. This is a different search direction from maximising the sum directly.
backlog.title: Successive-cap bisection on target sum

backlog.spec: After the restart loop ends, take the best (c, r) and run scipy.optimize.minimize with method='COBYLA' on the stacked vector v = [c.ravel(), r], objective -sum(r), using the same pair, wall and nonnegativity inequality constraints as _solve_once, with rhobeg=1e-3, tol=1e-12 and maxiter=2000. Pass the result through _repair and keep it only if its radius sum exceeds the incumbent's. This adds a gradient-free local solver at the end of the search, so it can escape SLSQP's stationary points where constraint Jacobians are degenerate. Budget it as 10% of TIME_FRACTION * time_limit, taken from the restart loop.
backlog.title: COBYLA derivative-free polish of the final incumbent

backlog.spec: Repeat a few times: draw a random unit direction d in the 2n-dimensional centre space from rng, and for t in a small grid (e.g. -0.05 to 0.05 in 9 steps) set centres to clip(c_best + t*d, 0, 1) and compute the best LP-optimal or greedy-repaired radii at fixed centres. Keep the t with the largest radius sum, then run the usual SLSQP cap continuation from that point with the radii as the start. This is a one-dimensional exploration of the basin boundary that is cheap compared with a full random restart and is not a Gaussian perturbation family, since the direction is shared by all coordinates along one line.
backlog.title: Random-direction line search through the incumbent

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centre start in _solve_once for a random half of the restarts by a Shirley-Chiu map of uniform points on the unit disc: sample u, v uniform on [0,1], map to the square [-1,1]^2 and then to a disc-shaped set, and rescale to [0.1, 0.9]^2 with a uniform random rotation. This gives a rounder, centre-weighted start that differs in shape from the square-uniform start. Keep the radius start, the cap schedule and the repair unchanged, and use the same rng for every draw so that seeds are reproducible.
backlog.title: Shirley-Chiu disc-to-square start distribution

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, after each cap stage compute the number of active contacts, meaning pair constraints with |d - r_i - r_j| < 1e-6 plus wall contacts with |wall gap| < 1e-6. If the active count is identical for two consecutive stages and the radius sum changed by less than 1e-4, skip the remaining cap stages and jump directly to the cap 1.0 stage. Track the number of restarts that finish early and report it only in a debug variable. The aim is to spend the freed CPU time on more restarts, since many late stages change almost nothing.
backlog.title: Contact-count stopping rule for the cap continuation

incumbent.description: Adds a radius-cap continuation to each SLSQP restart: caps rise from 0.05 to 0.4 in steps of 0.02 with warm starts, then a final solve at cap 1.0 (effectively uncapped).
